text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower across the board and settled around the day's lows. August closed $1.10 easier at $312.00 per tonne, while October gave up $0.30 to close at $304.50 per tonne. There was no fresh news to influence prices. Raw sugar futures in New York closed easier with front month May losing 17 points to close at 11.32 cents/lb, while July closed 4 points easier at 11.03 cents/lb. The May/July spread tightened to 29 points from 42 points at Monday's close.

The May contract expires on April 30 and speculators are still holding long positions. Bad news came from Egypt where the state's Sugar and Integrated Industries Company and private Egyptian sugar importers have agreed to resell some of their Brazilian raw sugar contracts because of a surplus. Egyptian companies have contracted about 500,000 tonnes of raws but there is already so much white sugar on the market that the sugar company cannot even sell the sugar it has refined from domestic production, it was said.

BRAZIL - Brazilian sugar exports should total 5.4 million tonnes, tel quel, according to the 1997/98 crop plan to be published on April 30, official sources said. This compares to 5.2 million tonnes in the 1996/97 and 4.033 million tonnes in the 1995/96 crop plan. Despite expectations of higher sugar cane output, the export target is only slightly higher than in the 1996/97 crop plan which is ascribed to the government's plan to use the extra sugar cane production to increase alcohol output. This year the government wants to boost alcohol production to the extent that imports are no longer necessary.

RUSSIA - Sucden-Moskva, a major importer of Cuban raw sugar into Russia, plans to import 400,000 tonnes of raws in 1997 against around 250,000 tonnes in 1996, Russian press reports said. Sucden-Moskva, part of French sugar group Sucden Kerry, said it did not intend to increase the amount of sugar it imported to Russia this year beyond 400,000 tonnes, despite a rise in sugar prices on Russia's domestic market. It was said loading capacity limits at Russian ports was a constraining factor, as was the high cost of transporting sugar by sea.

INDIA - Indian sugar production up to the end of March reached 10.745 million tonnes, white value, 8.8 per cent less than the 11.785 million tonnes produced the same period in 1995/96. Total production in 1996/97 is now estimated at 13.225 million tonnes, 3.226 million tonnes less than was produced in 1995/96. The decline is mainly a result of the dry conditions in Maharashtra where production is forecast to fall to 3.600 million tonnes, down from 5.395 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. Estimated production in 1996/97 of 13.2 million tonnes coupled with the prospect of another fall next season will put considerable strain on the availability of levy sugar.

As against an opening stock of 1.3 million tonnes for 1996/97, the closing stock is likely to be no more than 600,000 tonnes, meaning a shortfall of 700,000 tonnes whereas 1.3 million tonnes should be the barest minimum levy opening stock, informed sources said. It is expected that the government could either change the levy/free market ratio, currently at 40:60 per cent, or even ask the industry for sugar loans.

The industry has already opposed both proposals. However, the industry suggested that the government should buy some sugar on the open market and sell it in the 'fair price shops.' An alternative would be that the government imports sugar as long as prices are soft to cover the deficit.
